title: Why Is SK Hynix Stock Crashing, and is it a Buying Opportunity? | SKHY Stock Analysis
creator: Parkevtate Vosianc CFA
source_note: Detailed summary generated from video captions
summary: Parkevtate Vosianc examines SK Hynix after the stock fell from about $200 to about $120 on fears that anti-AI legislators and data-centre regulation will slow builds, compounded by Jensen Huang's resignation and export-control scrutiny. Q3 was strong: revenue up 32% quarter over quarter and 328% year over year, an 80% operating margin with record operating profit, high-bandwidth-memory mass production started, DRAM prices up in the high-20% range and storage up mid-20%. Management expects supply constraints until 2030; cloud capex is projected to grow more than 60% in 2027 and AI data-centre infrastructure about 40% a year to 2030. He notes only Micron has also posted operating margins above 80%. Cloud giants Alphabet, Microsoft and Amazon all signalled substantially higher capex. Valuation: a forward P/E of just 2.9. His DCF fair value is $254 against about $120. Call: SKHY BUY first tracked at about $120, conviction upgraded low to medium. Bull: capex growth extends the memory shortage. Bear: US regulation slows data-centre builds and new capacity from late 2027 compresses margins.

calls.thesis: BUY first tracked, conviction upgraded low to medium. SK Hynix fell from ~$200 to ~$120 on AI-regulation fears, but Q3 revenue was +32% QoQ / +328% YoY with an 80% operating margin, supply constrained until 2030, and a forward P/E of just 2.9 — a bargain valuation for a business firing on all cylinders.
calls.base_case: Memory supply shortage persists and prices stay elevated; management expects supply constraints until 2030.
calls.bull_case: Cloud capex grows 60%+ in 2027 and AI data-centre infrastructure grows ~40%/yr until 2030, extending the shortage.
calls.bear_case: US AI regulation slows data-centre builds and new capacity from late 2027 compresses margins and memory prices.
